problems.title: Edge direction
problems.statement: "[a, b] means b must be taken before a."
hints: Edges point from prerequisite to dependant.
problems.solution: b → a, and indeg[a] += 1. Reversing it silently produces reversed orders.

problems.title: Smallest order
problems.statement: n = 5, prerequisites [[1, 0], [2, 0], [3, 1], [3, 2], [4, 3]] in the [a, b] = "b before a" convention.
problems.solution: Order 0 1 2 3 4; 4 layers, since the longest chain is 0 → 1 → 3 → 4.

problems.title: Cycle detection
problems.statement: Kahn's algorithm on n = 6 places only 3 nodes before the frontier empties.

options: The remaining 3 nodes are on a cycle or depend on one

hints: No in-degree-0 node is left among them.
problems.solution: Every unplaced node has an unplaced predecessor. Following predecessors among finitely many nodes must repeat, so there is a cycle (and possibly nodes downstream of it).

problems.title: Three colours
problems.statement: In DFS cycle detection, a node is grey while it is on the current recursion path.

parts.prompt: An edge to a grey node means…
options: a cross edge, which is harmless

parts.prompt: An edge to a black (finished) node means…

hints: Grey = an ancestor on the current path.
problems.solution: A grey target is an ancestor, so the edge closes a cycle. Black nodes are fully explored and can't reach back onto the current path, or they would have found a grey node.

problems.title: Alien constraints
problems.statement: Sorted alien words: baa, abcd, abca, cab, cad.
hints: Compare each adjacent pair at its first mismatch.
problems.solution: Adjacent pairs give bbdac.

problems.title: Prefix rule
problems.statement: Which inputs are invalid in the alien dictionary?
hints: A word can't come after its own proper prefix; constraints can't form a cycle.
problems.solution: "abc" before "ab" breaks the prefix rule; a<b and b<a is a cycle; equal words give nothing.

problems.title: DAG longest path
problems.statement: Tasks with durations A = 3, B = 2, C = 4, D = 1; A before C, B before C, C before D. Independent tasks run in parallel.
hints: Relax in topological order: finish(v) = duration(v) + max finish of its predecessors.
problems.solution: finish(A) = 3, finish(B) = 2, finish(C) = 4 + max(3, 2) = 7, finish(D) = 8. The critical path is A → C → D.

problems.title: Heap frontier
problems.statement: Why does Kahn with a min-heap give the lexicographically smallest order?

options: At each position, any valid order must place an available node; the heap places the smallest, and doing so never removes options later

problems.solution: Taking the smallest available node v first can't block anything: every node available now stays available. So a smaller first element is always achievable, and induction finishes the proof.
